claims.text: A 19th-century town hall in Limoges, France, was damaged in an apparent arson attack on Saturday following nationwide protests.
Firefighters in Limoges fought the town hall blaze through Saturday night into Sunday morning.
Nationwide cost-of-living protests in France drew an estimated 550,000 demonstrators, according to authorities.
Unrest across France resulted in the deaths of two people: a 22-year-old police officer struck by a vehicle in Nantes and a protester near Paris.
French authorities reported around 2,400 arrests following nationwide clashes between protesters and police.

French President Emmanuel Macron stated in a televised address on Sunday: "Those who destroyed must pay. Those who looted must pay back. Those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable."
French President Emmanuel Macron blamed radical far-left factions and criminal elements for the destruction during the protests.
France's interior ministry reported that almost 1,000 police officers and gendarmes were injured during Saturday's unrest, with seven seriously hurt.
French police fired tear gas and stun grenades at hundreds of people gathered at Place de la République in Paris on Sunday.
Saturday's protests in France brought together trade unions, the anti-Macron Yellow Vests movement, and school students.
US President Donald Trump posted on social media blaming immigration for the unrest in France, stating "France is burning!"
Protests over cost of living and public services also took place in Spain, Italy, and Portugal.
Police in Paris reported a record 855 people were arrested in the French capital alone.
Limoges Mayor Guillaume Guérin stated that municipal police ran out of ammunition around 3:30 p.m. while trying to hold off rioters, calling it a "colossal failure of the state".
A fast-moving fire and subsequent explosion occurred at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta during a military training exercise on Saturday.
Four Canadian service members were killed and 39 patients were admitted to hospitals, with at least 19 in critical condition.
The four deceased service members were identified as Sgt Morgan Wong, Pte Shaun Farrell, Pte Aidan Goulding, and Pte Hayden Lykkemark.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney described the incident as "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime."
Prime Minister Mark Carney ordered flags on all federal buildings across Canada to be flown at half-mast.
The Department of National Defence stated there were no indications that the fire at CFB Wainwright was a terrorist attack.

Major-General Wade Rutland stated that soldiers were conducting live-fire combat exercises when a grass fire ignited about 1 km away and shifted towards the administrative area of the range due to uncommonly strong winds.
Alberta's provincial health agency deployed 30 units directly into Wainwright, including 22 ground ambulances, six fixed-wing planes, and two helicopters.
Canadian Forces Base Wainwright typically has about 690 military personnel and 300 civilian workers on site on a given day.
Military medical personnel parachuted into the town of Wainwright shortly before midnight to help respond to the disaster.
Cathy Keane, an Ontario mayoral candidate, stated on Facebook that her eldest son was among the critically injured military personnel.
Internal military communications indicate that 31 people were very seriously injured in the fire, according to the Globe and Mail.
Masked Israeli settlers attacked a delegation of Belgian, French, and Polish diplomats, a French mayor, and Palestinian civilians near Taybeh on Saturday.
Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was hospitalized after being assaulted on Friday while covering a Palestinian olive harvest in the West Bank.
US diplomats, including Assistant Secretary of State Riley Barnes and US Ambassador to the Holy See Brian Burch, visited the Christian Palestinian village of Taybeh on Sunday.
US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee attended a settler conference in the West Bank on Sunday after publicly calling for those who attacked Heidi Levine to be jailed.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military blamed "Israeli rioters" for Saturday's attack on the diplomats.
Israeli human rights group Yesh Din recorded at least 170 settler attacks on Palestinians since September 27.
The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu issued a social media statement titled "Serious accusations require serious evidence" casting doubt on the accounts of the attack on diplomats.
Eyewitnesses reported that an attacker aggressively shouted "France, France" before pushing French Mayor Bernard Baudoux to the ground during Saturday's attack.
Settlers smashed a reinforced window of an SUV carrying European diplomats as the vehicle drove away.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned against a brewing "crisis" in the West Bank following recent settler attacks.
The West Bank is home to around 500,000 Israeli settlers and at least 3 million Palestinians.
